thread:
incidents-bot: PAGER: high regional steering anomaly detected — sudden spike in cross-region latencies and 5xxs for requests routed to eu-west2 from us-east1. alert_id=RTE-2026-3931 severity=sev2 :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: Assigned to alex (oncall). Escalation policy: network -> runtime.
alex (oncall): reading telemetry now. seeing latency jump ~200ms -> 700ms for a subset of clients, 1.8% 5xx increase. Any recent routing policy changes?
maria (netops): no policy pushes in last 30m. We have increased probe failures from eu-west2 -> us-east1 healthcheck group. Looks like heartbeat timeouts followed by rapid reroute decisions.
sam (runtime): runtimes show KV cache pressure on eu-west2 under the higher tail — but CPU/GPU are ok. Could be feedback from steering controller triggering bursty fanout.
priya (prodops): customer impact? Which tenants?
tilly (cs): observed since ~10:01UTC customers A and B reported degraded responses in EMEA region. CS has opened tickets.
alex (oncall): ok first mitigation: pause steering adjustments for affected policy to prevent oscillation. Maria can you apply a temporary hold on geo-steer reconvergence?
maria (netops): running: `kubectl -n infra exec -it steer-controller-0 -- /bin/sh -c "echo 'pause:true' > /etc/steer/policy/region-geo-42"` — will hold reconverge for 10m. Pushing patch now.
maria (netops): patch applied. controller reports policy paused for region-geo-42.
alex (oncall): good. Next, pin traffic for the affected prefixes to a known-good region to stop automatic steering. Suggest pin -> eu-west2-primary-fallback. Sam ok to accept short-term pin?
sam (runtime): yes. I'll create a pinned route with higher priority and TTL 60s. Command:```
api call: POST /routing/pins {"prefix":"/api/v1/*","target":"eu-west2-primary-fallback","ttl":60,"reason":"inc-3931236540 temporary pin to stop oscillation"}
```
sam (runtime): pin push confirmed. New routing rule id=pin-3931-01.
priya (prodops): confirm: this will stop steering controller from reassigning those flows while paused?
maria (netops): yes, pinned routes take precedence over normal steering. Controller honors pin until TTL expires or pin removed.
tilly (cs): letting impacted customers know: "We're seeing a routing instability affecting EMEA traffic, temporarily pinning traffic to a stable region while we investigate. ETA 10-20 minutes."
alex (oncall): good. Now need to flush any edge DNScaches that may still be steering clients incorrectly. Maria, can you coordinate a soft DNS drain for the affected edge nodes?
maria (netops): scheduling soft drain — set `serve=0` on eu-edge-13, eu-edge-17 for 2m to force client re-resolve. Command: `edgectl drain --soft eu-edge-13,eu-edge-17 --duration 120s`
maria (netops): drain started. Observing fewer handoffs. healthchecks recovering.
sam (runtime): runtime logs showing decreased KV thrash after pin + drain. 5xx rate dropping back toward baseline.
priya (prodops): any signs of config bug causing the probe flaps?
maria (netops): preliminary: probes to us-east1 were intermittently timing out due to a route flap on a transit peer between regions — transit ASN X was dropping packets during heavy loads causing probe jitter. We have a ticket open with cloud provider NOC.
alex (oncall): escalate to provider and request RFO. Also create postmortem signal: timeline capture and probe graphs.
priya (prodops): creating incident record INC-3931236540, adding timeline items. Triage severity stays at sev2 unless we see customer-wide outages.
tilly (cs): Customers A & B acknowledged the update and will hold. Tilly -> CS will send a follow-up if recovery exceeds 20m.
sam (runtime): rolling back aggressive client-side retry heuristics for eu-west2 for a short window to reduce load amplification. Patch ID: rtry-3931-lite. Deployed to edge pool.
alex (oncall): monitoring for 5xx and p50/p95. If 5xx > 1.5% again, we escalate to sev1.
maria (netops): provider responded: "We see transient packet loss on PEER-X between 09:56-10:04UTC, mitigation in progress (BGP dampening tweak)." They suggest route stabilization in ~10m.
priya (prodops): ETA aligns with our pause TTL. Plan after stabilization: remove pin, run canary for 5m, then resume steering.
alex (oncall): agree. Post-mitigation checklist: 1) keep pin in place 2) monitor for 10m after provider OK 3) remove pin and pause flag, 4) run canary at 1% traffic for 5m then ramp. Assign owners: remove pin -> sam, unpause steer -> maria, customer comms -> tilly, postmortem -> priya.
sam (runtime): noted. I'll schedule pin removal at 10:18UTC unless we see regression.
maria (netops): will unpause after provider confirmation.
tilly (cs): sending final update to impacted customers: "Temporary routing pin applied, monitoring recovery. No request replay needed. We'll follow up with root cause when available."
incidents-bot: UPDATE: 5xx rate is down to +0.4% over baseline, p95 down to +90ms. incident state: mitigated (deg).
alex (oncall): handoff: I'm going offline for 20m, leaving sam as active owner. Pager on-call will monitor. If anything spikes, page me.
pagerduty-bot: Handoff acknowledged. On-call now: sam (runtime).
sam (runtime): I'll keep watching metrics and coordinate with maria for unpause. Adding logs/commands used to the incident record.
priya (prodops): adding timeline: pause at 10:02, pin at 10:04, dns drain 10:06, provider note 10:12, mitigation observed 10:14.
incidents-bot: Closing note: schedule a short postmortem to review steering controller backoff heuristics and probe timeout sensitivity.
tilly (cs): capturing customer feedback now, will include impact window in postmortem.
alex (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll review the postmortem draft later tonight.
file_description: Slack thread for a cross-region routing steering incident with paging, on-call coordination, temporary pinning and mitigations
